messages:
sophie: Heads-up — saw a p99 spike on the hosted canary for the text-gen route. Happens during a subset of requests with very long prompts + tool calls. dumping profiler, can someone pair on root cause? :eyes:
perf-bot: ALERT p99 latency increased 1200ms -> 2400ms over 5m window for route /v1/generate (canary)
raj: which model variant + quantization? any kernel fallbacks in the trace? also want KV cache hit rate around those requests
toni: throwing my 2c: we previously saw tool-calling loops cause repeated prefix growth and KV thrash — small % of requests can blow up seq_len and change kernel selection. worth checking seq_len distribution in the sample
sophie: profiler snippet from the offending trace (trimmed):
```
[profile] seq_len=4096 -> chosen_kernel=matmul_generic_fp32
[kernel_switch] reason=unsupported_block_size_for_fp16
[latency] total=2.34s  token_gen=1.9s  kv_evictions=14
```
looks like kernel fallback to generic fp32 happened after seeing long context. also saw kv_evictions spike
luis: kv stats for the canary window: `kv_cache_hits=92%, kv_cache_evictions=13, hot_prefix_reuse=0.7%` — evictions concentrated on requests with system+tools stacks
raj: ok that matches. kernel selection code picks optimized fp16 kernels only up to certain block sizes; when seq_len or head_count crosses threshold we fallback. two levers: 1) force different kernel selection heuristics based on observed seq_len distribution, 2) batching policy: reduce microbatch size for large-seq requests so they don't trigger heavy kernels concurrently
sophie: tried an A/B override: force kernel=optimized_fp16 for the model (hacky) — p95 slightly better but saw correctness regressions on very long prompts (bad perf on rare cases)
toni: also confirm tool loops: some prompt shapes keep appending tool responses in a loop (eg user asks tool to fetch->tool returns function call->model re-invokes tool). That steadily increases context and trashes the cache. we should detect repeated tool-call patterns and short-circuit after n iterations
raj: microbatch experiment: set microbatch_max_tokens=8000 and max_microbatch=1 for long-seq requests detected by header `x-est-seqlen`. result: p95 improved from 320ms -> 210ms, throughput dropped ~20% and p99 still had 2-3 outliers at ~1.2s
sophie: posted a short script we used to tag long requests in the router:
```
if est_seqlen > 2048:
  route = "long_ctx_fastpath"
  microbatch.max=1
  cache.pin_prefix=true
```
that reduced KV evictions for pinned prefixes
luis: evictions after pinning: `kv_cache_evictions=2` in the experiment window, hot_prefix_reuse=9% (was 0.7%)
eva: ops suggestion: add a protection that caps tool calls per request (max_tool_calls=3) and a defensive prompt-shortener for generated tool outputs > 512 tokens. This avoids runaway loops without changing model kernels. We can gate via rollout flag for canary customers
sophie: combining microbatch routing + pinning + tool-call cap: short canary results: p95 210ms, p99 890ms, throughput -18%. looks promising as a stop-gap. need long canary to validate quality regressions and edge cases :thinking:
perf-bot: CANARY RUN (post-fix) summary: p95=210ms p99=890ms errors=0.3% throughput_delta=-18%
sophie: great. next steps: 1) bake kernel-selection telemetry (emit reason code when fallback happens), 2) implement seqlen-aware batching in router, 3) add tool-call guard + prefix pinning, 4) run 24h canary and follow with a short write-up for the infra perf board. will schedule pairing tomorrow AM. :rocket:
